I'll think this through as the farmer would.

---

My name is... well, that's not important. I've been working this land for 20 years. My husband helps, and my older son too when he's not away working. We have 10.1 mu total. Let me think about how I'll split it this year like I did last year.

I plant cotton on about 2 mu — that back piece near the road where the soil is a bit sandier. Cotton does okay there and the price has been decent. The other 8 mu is my wheat-maize land, good flat ground with the well nearby. Wheat in winter, maize in summer, same as always. With 7 mouths to feed, we eat some of the wheat flour ourselves and sell the rest. The maize mostly goes to sell, some we keep for the chickens.

**For my wheat (8 mu):**
Last year I got about 450 kg per mu, which was alright — the year before was better, maybe 480, because the rains came at the right time. I use the improved seed from the dealer in town, "Jimai" something — I forget the exact number but it's the one most people around here plant. I buy a new bag every 2-3 years.

For fertilizer, before plowing I put down about 50 kg of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 bag) per mu as base fertilizer. That's one bag per mu basically. Then at green-up in spring I top-dress with urea, about 20 kg per mu. So that gives me maybe 17-18 kg of nitrogen per mu total, 7-8 kg phosphorus, 7-8 kg potassium. Same as what my neighbor Old Wang does, and he gets good wheat.

I water the wheat 3 times usually — once before winter (the freezing water), once at green-up, and once at heading. If spring is dry I might add one more. The well is close so water isn't a big worry, just the electricity cost.

I plow with the tractor service the village has — rotary tilling after maize harvest, it's fastest. Spray for aphids once or twice in spring, and once for the disease on the heads before flowering. That's 2-3 times with the pesticide.

**For my maize (8 mu, after wheat):**
After we harvest wheat in June, the tractor comes and we plant maize right away — "Zhengdan 958" or similar hybrid, the seed company sells it. No plowing, we direct-seed with the machine. Got about 550 kg per mu last year.

I put compound fertilizer in the furrow when planting, about 40 kg per mu (the 15-15-15 again or sometimes a higher-nitrogen one). Then when the maize is knee-high I top-dress urea, maybe 25 kg per mu. So about 18-20 kg nitrogen per mu, 6 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium.

Maize needs water 2 times mostly — once after the top-dressing, once when the tassel comes out. If July rains are good I skip one. Spray once for the borer worm, maybe twice if I see a lot of them. So 1-2 sprays.

**For my cotton (2 mu):**
Cotton is more work than wheat-maize, but the price is better per kg. I use the hybrid Bt cotton seed — you almost have to, otherwise the bollworm eats everything. I plow this field properly with the plough because cotton likes deeper loose soil.

Fertilizer: base fertilizer about 40 kg of compound per mu before planting, then top-dress urea twice — once at squaring, once at flowering, about 15 kg each time. So nitrogen about 20 kg per mu, phosphorus 6, potassium 6. Cotton really wants the nitrogen to keep making bolls.

Water 3 times — once before squaring, once at flowering, once when bolls are filling. I spray pesticide a lot on cotton, maybe 5-6 times through the season — for aphids early, spider mites in hot weather, and the plant-bugs. Even with Bt seed you still have to spray for other pests. Last year I got about 230 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I won't change much this year. What I do works. Maybe if the fertilizer price goes up too much I'll cut the urea top-dress on maize a little, but I'd rather spend the money than lose yield — a bad harvest with 7 people to feed is a real problem.
